Use case: precise-object-edit / battle-effect family. One isolated scalable still on a square 1024x1024 canvas, no background or other artwork. Exact contact point at canvas center. Preserve clear, unpainted transparent margins and transparent gaps. Bold clean silhouette readable at120px over warm amber interiors and moonlit blue sea. No full-canvas wash, checkerboard pixels, character, body parts, weapons, ground, shadow, lettering, labels, numbers, watermark, blood, red, neon, fire or scene. Do not crop the canvas.
Target: HIT-1, a SMALL glancing knock. Replace the pointed starburst with a soft compact irregular rounded ivory dust puff, lightly amber in its interior and inked along its uneven cloud-like rim. A few rounded lobes, two or three tiny short brush ticks to suggest a light bump. No sharp large rays, ring or dramatic debris. The whole puff and every tiny tick occupies only the central 50-55% of canvas width and height. It must be visibly gentler and smaller than the reference at exactly the same canvas size. It conveys a harmless moment of force and surprise, not smoke from a fire. The puff center is exactly the contact point.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: ONE production-ready transparent 2D game battle-effect sprite, medium impact HIT-2, for CosyWorld's hand-painted storybook card-table squabbles.
Generate one isolated compact starburst at peak impact. Square 1024x1024 RGBA canvas, genuinely transparent background. No environment, character, fist, weapon, floor or shadow. The exact impact center is the canvas center. Keep all paint, detached chips and ink marks within the central 70 percent of the canvas with generous completely clear padding on all four sides. Do not crop or trim.
Silhouette: an irregular, lively seven-to-nine-point ivory pressure star, a compact burst of force and surprise; broad brush-painted warm amber wedges inside; six or fewer distinct small soot ink splashes or angular flecks outside. Bold simple shapes, one coherent burst. A rough hand-inked deep brown-black outer contour and pale ivory fill must both remain readable when the sprite is shown only 120 pixels across over a warm amber attic or dark blue night sea.
Style: exquisite restrained storybook fantasy ink-and-gouache, slightly ragged dry-brush contours, visibly loose painterly washes inside the shape, matching delicately inked warm fantasy character portraits. Ivory, warm honey amber, soot black, a very small muted blue-grey shadow accent. Matte pigment, not glossy or vector-flat. Transparent gaps between rays and around every fleck. No full-canvas wash, no ambient glow rectangle, no photographic texture backdrop.
No blood, red, gore, injuries, fire, explosion cloud, smoke background, neon, lens flare, letters, numbers, icons inside the burst, watermarks, frames, text, checkerboard pixels or labels. This is a scalable still, not a sheet of frames. Preserve clean real alpha transparency and all negative space.

Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: CosyWorld combat overlay, brace-raise, one transparent square production sprite.
Input image 1 is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: copy its tactile hand-inked, matte gouache brushwork, ragged dark soot contours and warm ivory contrast, not its burst shape or orange fire.

Create ONE intact frontal protective shield effect, centered exactly at canvas coordinates (0.5, 0.5). A simple broad rounded top, gently narrowing sides and one modest pointed bottom; a bold recognizable shield silhouette with no heraldry. This is a painted translucent barrier, not a metallic prop. Its irregular soot-black outer contour and slim warm-ivory inner edge should read over either a warm amber attic or a dark blue sea. Inside the rim, use a desaturated moonlight-blue translucent wash with subtle dry-brush texture: genuinely partly transparent pigment, no solid blue background panel. Restrained and reassuring, ready to absorb a blow. No damage, cracks, impact, ripples or broken pieces yet.

Composition: square canvas. The shield's full visible paint, including all ragged edges, fits within the central 70–75 percent of the canvas height; its width is around 55–60 percent. Maintain completely transparent space on all four sides, never less than 6.25 percent of the canvas on any edge. Keep it upright, facing the viewer straight on, no perspective tilt. Balanced around the exact center, with even visual padding; no cropped paint. Bold few-part design readable when reduced to 120 pixels, and complete as one still frame.

Medium: the reference's storybook soot ink and handmade matte gouache, irregular painterly edges, gentle ivory highlight and cool pale-blue wash. No photorealism, glossy 3D, chrome, neon or smooth vector geometry. A cosy fantasy squabble effect, no gore.

CRITICAL: genuine transparent alpha background, including all outside space. Do not paint black, white, coloured, gradient, paper or checkerboard backing. Preserve semitransparency in the shield's blue interior. No people, body parts, weapons, handles, straps, ornaments, letters, numbers, runes, symbols, caption, border, floor, environment, cast shadow, glow cloud, sparks or additional effects. Output one single centered shield sprite only.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset: corrected brace-absorb transparent combat sprite.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and exact shape/alpha master: brace-raise, the pale-blue intact shield with genuinely translucent blue wash.
Input image 2 is ONLY the ripple-and-short-cracks reference: the first brace-absorb version. Its blue face became almost opaque; do NOT copy that opacity.

Make a precise correction: start from image 1 and add the contained central compression ripple from image 2 while retaining image 1's semi-transparent blue face. SAME exact square canvas, shield silhouette, size, center, soot-black contour, ivory border, pointed top/bottom, curved shoulders and original hand-painted texture. No camera, outline or positioning change. The face should carry the two broad curved ivory/blue ripple arcs and three short fine central cracks of image 2, clearly distinguishable at small game size, without breaking the rim or creating a hole. No fragments.

The crucial deliverable is REAL PARTIAL ALPHA in the blue face, not a painted impression of transparency. The blue interior must remain a thin translucent wash through which the eventual game background will be visible, like image 1: aim at alpha about 150–190/255 across broad blue areas; keep the dark outer contour and warm ivory rim strongly opaque. Let the ripple crest be a delicate higher-opacity stroke over the translucent wash, not an opaque white or blue sheet covering the face. The current correction is specifically to remove the unwanted almost-opaque blue fill from image 2. Preserve the original matte gouache colour and texture; no glass rendering, no glossy highlights, no neon glow.

Outside the shield preserve actual transparent alpha. Every pixel of the outermost 8 percent of the square canvas must be fully alpha zero: no stray translucent speckles. No black, white, coloured, paper, gradient or checkerboard background. No text, letters, runes, symbols, heraldry, people, body parts, weapon, floor, environment, shadow, extra spark or new object. One frontal shield only, as a complete still, exact matched framing to image 1.
